The aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeals are being disposed of by this common order as they arise from the same award.

2. M.A. No.6479/2019 is filed by the claimants on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of amount of compensation and M.A.No.5981/2019 is filed by the Insurance Company for reduction of compensation.
3.
These appeals have been filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 26.08.2019 passed by Member MACT, Shajapur in Claim CaseNo.51/2018.
4. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
in case of death of Balbir Singh, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,16,600/-
along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realisation.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

The deceased was a skilled labour hence the compensation must be calculated on the basis of circular of the Labour Commissioner under the Minimum Wages Act which comes to Rs.9,360/-.
6.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that deceased was not a skilled labour and he was an Assistant of the Halwai hence he was admittedly a permanent employee and was self employed.
So Tribunal has assessed the income on the higher side and prays for reduction of compensation.

7. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants stated that the deceased was working as Halwai.
So he is a skilled labour.
Perusal of the cross examination of AW-2 Dilip Saini Mali it is clearly established that deceased was not doing independent business, but he was the Assistant of Dilip Saini Mali.
The Tribunal in its award in para 16 held that deceased was the Assistant of main Halwai.
So the Tribunal has wrongly assessed that he was a skilled labour.
In the considered opinion of this Court, he was Assistant of the main Cook and deemed to be semi skilled labour.
According to the circular of the Labour Commissioner at the time of accident, the minimum wages of a semi skilled labour was Rs.7,982/- per month.
Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation must be assessed on the basis of income of deceased as Rs.7,982/- per month.
9. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that according to the postmortem report the deceased was 32 years old and multiplier of 16 must be applied instead of 17.

But perusal of the record of the Tribunal, it is found that claimants filed Aadhar Card of the deceased in which the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1987 so it must be calculated on the basis of Aadhar card instead of the postmortem report.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has rightly assessed his age and applied the multiplier of 17.
Hence, there is no need of interference in regard to this finding of the Tribunal.

10. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased in M.A.No.6479/2019for calculating the compensation amount is as under:
Income of the claimant(Permanent Rs.7,982/-P.M. + Rs.3192/- (40% Disability)
FP)=Rs.11,174/ less Rs.5,587/- (1/2 for personal expenses) x12 x 17 =Rs.Rs.11,39,748-  Consortium Rs.80,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

Total Amount Rs.12,49,748/-
11.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in M.A.No.6479/2019 is Rs.12,49,748/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.11,16,600/-.

Accordingly,
the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,33,148/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
12. In the result, the appeal (M.A.No.5981/2019) filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
The appeal (M.A.No.6479/2019) filed by the appellants/claimants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
